content.text: You’ve written an ebook. You’re ready to sell it. But in Kenya, Stripe and PayPal are not options. Conventional platforms reject you. This is not a problem to workaround—it’s a signal to build better [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-selling-design-assets-crypto-payments-4|The Full]]. Your solution must be [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/sovereign-commerce-infrastructure-digital-creators-what-nobody-tells-16|sovereign]]. You need a commerce stack you own, not rent. This guide walks you through deploying a complete digital store using [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-explained-digital-13|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] infrastructure and blockchain payments. No platforms. No subscriptions. No geographic restrictions. By the end, you’ll have a live store that processes crypto payments automatically, delivers your ebook instantly, and stores your data securely—all without relying on third parties. This is not a temporary fix. It’s base-layer infrastructure designed to outlast payment blockades and currency instability. You own it. You control it. You scale it.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Platforms fail because they are centralized. Stripe and PayPal operate under regulatory frameworks that exclude entire regions. Your store cannot depend on them. Instead, you build on decentralized infrastructure. Cloudflare provides hosting and backend logic. Supabase stores orders. NOWPayments processes crypto payments. These tools are not platforms—they are components you assemble into a stack you own. Cloudflare’s global edge network ensures your store loads fast, everywhere. NOWPayments verifies transactions on-chain, eliminating chargebacks. Supabase gives you full data ownership. This architecture removes geographic barriers. It’s not a workaround for payment rejection—it’s a replacement for the systems that reject you. You deploy once, and the infrastructure runs without ongoing fees or platform dependencies. This is sovereignty, not access.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying, gather your assets. You need your ebook file, a domain name (optional but recommended), and a NOWPayments account. Your ebook should be finalized and tested. Use Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to store the file securely. For the domain, register one via Cloudflare or use a GitHub Pages default URL. Set up a NOWPayments account to accept crypto—choose low-fee networks like BSC, Solana, or TRON. You’ll also need a Cloudflare account for hosting and backend logic. If you’re using the Complete Builder Kit, you get all templates and blueprints instantly. No coding required. Your goal is to have all components ready before deployment. This ensures a seamless process. You’re not building from scratch—you’re assembling proven infrastructure.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Your pipeline has three parts: payment processing, order storage, and file delivery. Start with NOWPayments. Create a payment link for your ebook and configure the webhook to trigger delivery. Use Cloudflare Workers to handle backend logic—when payment confirms, the worker sends the ebook download link to the buyer. Store order data in Supabase or Google Sheets. For file delivery, upload your ebook to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Set permissions so the download link is temporary and secure. Test each component individually. Verify that payments trigger the webhook, the webhook fires the worker, and the worker delivers the file. This pipeline is automated. Once deployed, it runs without your intervention. You’re not managing transactions—you’re owning the infrastructure that manages them.
Your store runs on infrastructure you own—no platforms, no subscriptions.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Deploy your store using Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. Connect your domain if you have one. Test the entire flow: simulate a purchase, verify payment processing, and confirm file delivery. Use testnet crypto for trials. Once live, monitor your first real transaction. Check that the payment confirms on-chain, the webhook fires, and the buyer receives the ebook. If any step fails, review your logs. Cloudflare and NOWPayments provide detailed diagnostics. Your store is now operational. You’re not waiting for platform approvals or dealing with geographic restrictions. You’re selling directly to customers, anywhere in the world. This is sovereignty in action.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Your infrastructure is designed to scale. Add more products by replicating your pipeline. Use Supabase to manage inventory and order history. Configure email notifications via Cloudflare Workers for customer updates. If traffic increases, Cloudflare’s edge network handles it automatically. For higher volume, upgrade to paid tiers of Supabase or NOWPayments—but only when necessary. Your costs remain predictable. No platform fees. No revenue sharing. Scaling is a matter of adding components, not asking for permission. This is the advantage of owning your stack. You’re not limited by platform constraints. You’re building on infrastructure that grows with you.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

To sell ebooks from Kenya without Stripe or PayPal, deploy a sovereign commerce stack using Cloudflare infrastructure and blockchain payments. Use Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. Upload your ebook to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for secure delivery. This architecture removes geographic barriers and gives you full ownership of your store. No platforms. No subscriptions. Lifetime access.
Blockchain payments remove geographic barriers entirely.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, and other restricted markets searching for international payment solutions are looking for the same thing: a way to receive USD-equivalent payments from global buyers without a Stripe or PayPal account. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 is the complete answer — Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments deployed under your accounts in 48 hours. For creators who want to self-deploy, the Sovereign Blueprint at $47 covers both stack options with full source code and step-by-step configuration guides. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Finalize your ebook and upload it to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. 2. Register a domain (optional) and set up a Cloudflare account. 3. Create a NOWPayments account and configure a payment link for your ebook. 4. Deploy your store using Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. 5. Test the entire flow: payment, webhook, file delivery. 6. Monitor your first real transaction and verify all components work seamlessly.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this infrastructure if I’m not technical?
Yes. The Complete Builder Kit provides templates and blueprints that require no coding. Follow the step-by-step guides to deploy your store.
What cryptocurrencies can I accept?
NOWPayments supports 300+ cryptocurrencies. Recommended low-fee networks include BSC, Solana, and TRON—all under $0.10 per transaction.
Do I need to pay ongoing fees?
No. After deployment, you own the infrastructure. The only fee is NOWPayments’ 0.5% transaction charge.
Can I scale this to sell multiple products?
Yes. Replicate the pipeline for each product. Use Supabase to manage inventory and order history.
What if a payment fails?
NOWPayments provides detailed transaction logs. Review these to identify issues. Cloudflare Workers can send email notifications for failed payments.
Deploy once, scale indefinitely—this is sovereignty, not access.
